newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Brierley should receive S&P upgrade - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: Brierley should receive S&P upgrade - ANZ.

text.p: New Zealand-based Brierley Investments Ltd should receive a small credit upgrade from the Standard and Poor's Corp to BBB when the company is re-rated, ANZ Investments said.
The company was last rated by S&P in 1994, and its long term debt rating is expected to be reviewed in the third quarter of 1997, ANZ said.
The U.S. ratings agency currently rates the long-term debt of Brierley at BBB-minus and its short-term rating at A-3.
The main reason for the expected upgrade is the changes in its exposure to, and the profitability of, its Thistle Hotels investment in the United Kingdom, the research report said.

Brierley has recently tapped the medium term note (MTN) market, issuing A$200 million of five year notes, carrying an 8.10 percent coupon. ANZ said at the issue spread of 52 basis points over swap there was significant value in the securities versus similar stock.

As well, given the Brierley MTN documentation contained bank loan-style covenants and protection for bondholders, there was no structural reason for there to be any spread between the bilateral bank loan and MTN markets, ANZ said.

"As a result, we expect the Brierley spread to trade down to the bank market level (45 basis points over swap and 75 basis points over government bonds) leading up to and after the S&P review," the research report said.

Brierley is an investment company which has stakes in a number of leading Australian firms, including a 20 percent holding in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, 28 percent of building materials firm James Hardie Industries Ltd and 7.4 percent of retailer Coles Myer Ltd.
